question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{5}{4},$ we will set our result equal to $\frac{5}{4}.$ 

From the equation $y=(2x+3)(x-k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{2}$ and ${x}_{2}=k.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{3}{2}+k)}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{2k}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{2k-3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{5}{4}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2k-3}{4} & =\frac{5}{4} \\ 2k-3 & =5 \\ 2k & =8 \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
